guide_line: Add the atomic masses in a formula, then use that molar mass to move between grams and moles.
steps: 6.1 Formula Mass: add the atomic mass of every atom the formula shows. That sum is the formula mass in amu.
Call that sum a molecular mass only for a covalent molecule. An ionic compound has no molecules, so keep the name formula mass.
The same number in g/mol is the molar mass. One mole of the substance has that mass in grams.
Direction matters. Divide grams by the molar mass to get moles. Multiply moles by the molar mass to get grams. Divide a particle count by 6.022e23 to get moles.
A mole is 6.022×10^23 particles. Use 6.022e23 when you need a count to 4 significant figures.
Chain the units. Grams times (1 mol / molar mass in g) gives moles. Moles times the molar mass gives grams. Moles times 6.022e23 gives particles. Multiply by a subscript to count one element.

worked_example.q: How many molecules are in 4.500 g of water? H is 1.00794 and O is 15.9994. Use 6.022e23 per mole. Write the count as 1.504e23 molecules.

similar_problem.q: How many molecules are in 9.000 g of water? Use H 1.00794, O 15.9994, and 6.022e23 per mole.
similar_problem.hint: Divide 9.000 g by the water molar mass, about 18.02 g/mol, then multiply those moles by 6.022e23.

problems.q: What is the molar mass of NaHCO3? Use Na 22.989769, H 1.00794, C 12.011, and O 15.9994. Give 4 significant figures.
problems.why: NaHCO3 has one Na, one H, one C, and three O. 22.989769 + 1.00794 + 12.011 + 3(15.9994) = 84.0069 g/mol, which rounds to 84.01 g/mol.
hints: Add one sodium, one hydrogen, one carbon, and three oxygens. The three oxygens are the heavy part.

problems.q: What is the molar mass of Mg(NO3)2? Use Mg 24.305, N 14.0067, and O 15.9994. Give 4 significant figures.
problems.why: Two nitrate groups mean 2 N and 6 O. 24.305 + 2(14.0067) + 6(15.9994) = 148.3148 g/mol, which rounds to 148.3 g/mol.
hints: Count two nitrogens and six oxygens inside the two nitrate groups, then add one magnesium.

problems.q: How many moles are in 8.500 g of CO2? C is 12.011 and O is 15.9994. Give 4 significant figures.
hints: Build the CO2 molar mass from one C and two O, then divide 8.500 g by that mass.

problems.q: What is the mass of 0.2500 mol of CaCl2? Ca is 40.078 and Cl is 35.453. Give 4 significant figures.
hints: The formula has two chlorines. Multiply 0.2500 mol by the full CaCl2 molar mass.

problems.q: How many molecules are in 0.1800 mol of NH3? Use 6.022e23 per mole. Give 4 significant figures.
problems.why: The moles are already known. 0.1800 mol × (6.022e23 molecules / 1 mol) = 1.084e23 molecules.
hints: 0.1800 mol is already moles. Multiply by 6.022e23. Skip the molar mass.

problems.q: What is the mass of 2.500e22 molecules of H2O? H is 1.00794, O is 15.9994, and 1 mol is 6.022e23 molecules. Give 4 significant figures.
hints: Divide 2.500e22 by 6.022e23 to get moles of water, then multiply by about 18.02 g/mol.

problems.q: How many oxygen atoms are in 4.200 g of H2SO4? H is 1.00794, S is 32.066, and O is 15.9994. Use 6.022e23. Give 4 significant figures.
hints: H2SO4 has four oxygens. After moles of acid, multiply by 4 and then by 6.022e23.

problems.q: How many moles of Cl are in 5.000 g of CaCl2? Ca is 40.078 and Cl is 35.453. Give 4 significant figures.
problems.why: Molar mass = 110.984 g/mol. Moles of CaCl2 = 5.000 g × (1 mol / 110.984 g) = 0.04505 mol. Moles of Cl = 0.04505 mol × 2 = 0.09010 mol.
hints: Change 5.000 g of CaCl2 into moles, then multiply by the subscript 2.

problems.q: What mass of carbon is in 10.00 g of C6H12O6? C is 12.011, H is 1.00794, and O is 15.9994. Give 4 significant figures.
hints: Six carbons weigh 6 times 12.011 g in one mole of glucose. That fraction of 10.00 g is the carbon mass.

problems.q: How many atoms are in 3.400 g of Al? Al is 26.981539. Use 6.022e23 per mole. Give 4 significant figures.
hints: Divide 3.400 g by 26.981539 g/mol, then multiply by 6.022e23. Aluminum's subscript is 1.

problems.q: What is the mass of 1.250 mol of Fe2O3? Fe is 55.845 and O is 15.9994. Give 4 significant figures.
hints: Add two irons and three oxygens, then multiply that molar mass by 1.250 mol.

problems.q: How many moles of N are in 6.800 g of (NH4)2SO4? N is 14.0067, H is 1.00794, S is 32.066, and O is 15.9994. Give 4 significant figures.
hints: (NH4)2SO4 holds two nitrogens. Divide 6.800 g by the molar mass, then multiply by 2.

problems.q: CaCl2 is ionic, so it is not made of molecules. What two-word name is used for the sum of the atomic masses in its formula?
problems.why: Ionic compounds do not have molecules. The sum of the atomic masses in CaCl2 is the formula mass. The same number in g/mol is the molar mass.
hints: CaCl2 is ionic. Use the name that fits a formula of ions, not the name that says molecule.

problems.q: H2O is a covalent molecule. What two-word name is used for the sum of the atomic masses in that molecule?
problems.why: Water is made of molecules. The sum of the atomic masses in H2O is its molecular mass. That same number is also the formula mass and, in g/mol, the molar mass.
hints: H2O is a molecule. The name that includes the word molecular fits this sum.

problems.q: How many moles are in 3.011e24 atoms of Mg? Use 6.022e23 per mole. Give 4 significant figures.
problems.why: Moles = 3.011e24 atoms × (1 mol / 6.022e23 atoms) = 5.000 mol. The atomic mass is not used when the question starts from a count of atoms.
hints: 3.011e24 is a count of magnesium atoms. Divide by 6.022e23. The atomic mass 24.305 is not part of this step.

problems.q: How many moles are in 4.250e-3 g of P? P is 30.973762. Give 4 significant figures.
hints: 4.250e-3 g of phosphorus is the given mass. Divide by 30.973762 g/mol.
